review_method: Technical data-flow review, bound to the complete source-file SHA-256. Raw findings remain in reports; changed source or new rule IDs require a new review.

reviews.reason: UniqueSafeLoader subclasses yaml.SafeLoader and adds duplicate-key rejection and timestamp-as-text only. Unsafe tags, aliases, nesting and byte limits are tested; this is not yaml.UnsafeLoader.
Both matches are empty-string initialization/clearing of the in-memory OAuth cache. Actual access tokens come from the authenticated provider response; no credential is hard-coded.
The literals are mock-token-not-live and the Bearer protocol label in the explicit loopback mock. They do not authenticate to Microsoft or the private analyst API.

Assertions document already-enforced foreign-key or locked create/read postconditions. Route dependencies and explicit checks enforce authorization and existence before these points; removing assertions does not grant access.

The password match is an environment-reference name used only by the mock adapter. The assertion is a post-poll persisted-row invariant, not an authorization check; the connector was already loaded and connectors have no delete API.
checked_url has already explicitly rejected a missing hostname. The assertion narrows that established invariant; IP/network/TLS/redirect enforcement is not implemented with assert.

ElementTree is imported for Element type/ParseError only. Actual parsing calls defusedxml.fromstring with DTD/entity/external rejection, followed by depth/node bounds. Encoding-bypass regressions exercise the real parser.
test-only-public-demo-owner and the empty token are isolated TestClient inputs proving owner/reset and missing-token behavior; neither is a deployed credential.
test-only-value is a synthetic TestClient credential for a temporary database, never a real service secret.

Reviewed literals are a demo environment-reference name, synthetic-access/synthetic mock tokens, and intentionally empty/newline tokens used to verify rejection. Responses use a test transport, not a live identity service.
0.0.0.0 is a rejected-address test value, not a listener. Token literals are an environment-reference name and an explicitly synthetic redaction marker; no real credential is supplied.
SENTINEL_INTEGRATION_COLLECTOR names a test-provided environment variable, not its secret value.
local-test-token is an isolated authentication-error fixture, not an operational token.
The literal is an environment-reference name in a Pydantic expiry/schema test; it contains no authentication value.
The test invokes fixed local verification scripts with -O to prove disabled assertions fail before mutation. It uses argv lists, no shell and no telemetry-derived commands.

synthetic-local-probe exists only in a monkeypatched unit-test environment. urlopen is replaced by an in-memory fixture; the literal cannot authenticate to a real API, container or integration. The additional local .env copy contains only a synthetic marker and verifies owner-only artifact permissions.
A fixed OpenSSL argv generates an ephemeral test certificate/key under pytest's temporary directory. No event/HTTP input becomes executable; the key is chmod 0600 and not committed.
The test asserts the intended container/Render listen configuration using a mocked launcher; it does not bind a public listener.
The assertion narrows a metrics value produced by a validated nonempty iteration loop, not an access-control decision.

This verification probe refuses optimized Python and intentionally asserts actual kernel/API results. HTTP targets are constructed in-container loopback URLs with an integer port; the container has no external network.

Launches only Python/Uvicorn and locally installed Vite using argv lists. Environment ports are converted to integers and bind-checked. Trusted operator PATH/configuration is not remotely supplied telemetry; no shell interpretation occurs.
Seed 7341 deliberately reproduces inert fuzz fixture structure. This PRNG never generates credentials, signatures, authentication nonces or identifiers requiring secrecy.
Generator invariant for locally authored deterministic fixture counts. It is not runtime authorization or untrusted code execution.

Fixed repository development/test commands are selected by argparse choices and executed as argv without a shell. The Python override is an explicit trusted operator executable choice, not event/API data.
Optional reproduction downloads only fixed HTTPS URLs at a pinned OTRF revision, checks archive bytes/size/hash, reads a named member in memory, and never executes or extracts telemetry.

The owner-selected CLI API URL is explicitly restricted to HTTP(S), hostname present and no credentials/query/fragment. It is not an inbound SSRF endpoint. The assertion narrows a run after nonempty validated telemetry; no authorization depends on assert.

Owned-process verification refuses -O, executes fixed local argv, and generates ephemeral credentials rather than hard-coding them. The token literal is an environment-reference name. /tmp is an isolated, size-bounded container tmpfs, not a shared host temporary file.

Fixed local Git inspection/hash commands bind source/media evidence; argv lists are used without a shell. Git comes from the trusted assessment host PATH, not uploaded telemetry. The gate is operator-run tooling, not an API execution surface.

Local scanner/Git argv never invokes a shell or accepts log commands. Scanners are pinned and locally installed; Git uses trusted operator PATH. Public-key triage restricts the Git object to a hexadecimal commit and eight exact evidence/test paths. The empty Semgrep token disables hosted analysis; no credential is embedded.

The optional installer accepts only approved publisher HTTPS prefixes; native downloads are SHA-256 verified before execution, archives are not extracted wholesale, and Python tools install from a hash lock with fixed argv and no shell.

0.0.0.0 is the required container/Render listener, not an authentication bypass. Host/origin/owner/public-mode boundaries remain enforced, proxy-header trust is disabled, and local rehearsal publishes only loopback ports.

Fixed repository test/build argv is executed without a shell. The assertion checks stdout=PIPE's postcondition, not authorization. The validator refuses optimized Python and requires real executed, non-skipped tests.

Operator-run rehearsal refuses -O, uses fixed argv and validated numeric ports/labels, and sends HTTP only to constructed loopback URLs. /tmp denotes a bounded in-container tmpfs. Assertions are intentional executable verification, not production permissions; only owned processes/volumes are stopped.

Trace ends at fixed Uvicorn/Vite argv; environment port strings are parsed as integers and checked by bind. There is no shell or telemetry-to-command flow. Choosing an executable through the local operator's PATH is an explicit development-host trust boundary.
The matched call launches the installed Vite script using argv, an integer port and an operator-controlled environment. No shell interpretation or remote event input reaches the executable/arguments.
